podcast.title: Corpse Paint Aesthetics (1974)
podcast.body: As the singer of the fictional band The Undead in the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' Peter Ibling was depicted in "corpse paint," a visual style noted for its resemblance to modern death metal or black metal makeup, which contributes to the theory of the film being proto-goth or proto-death metal. "The singer of the Undead is a dude named Peter Ebling. He is made up in corpse paint, and I like what you would see with modern death metal or black metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Corpse Paint in Phantom of the Paradise (1974)
podcast.body: Peter Ebling, the singer of the fictional band The Undead in the 1974 film "Phantom of the Paradise," is depicted wearing corpse paint similar to what would later be seen in modern death metal or black metal. This early use of corpse paint contributes to the theory that the film contained elements of proto-goth or proto-death metal.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Proto-Goth/Death Metal Visuals
xref.body: The Undead, a fictional band from the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' featured its singer, Peter Ibling, and the rest of the band made up in "corpse paint," a visual style compared to modern death metal or black metal, suggesting proto-goth or proto-death metal aesthetics. "The singer of the Undead is a dude named Peter Ebling. He is made up in corpse paint, and I like what you would see with modern death metal or black metal."
